In a study of marine behavior, Dr. Sarangerel Dorj and colleagues presented dolphins with floating hoops and observed many of the animals leaping through, spinning around, and tossing the objects to one another. The dolphins simply appeared to be playing—and for no other reason than because they were experiencing joy.

Dolphins lack the prefrontal structures and neural pathways linked to complex emotions in primates. Nevertheless, Dorj and her team have demonstrated that dolphins may engage in recreational behavior, potentially experiencing some form of positive psychological state. Previous research has documented that dolphins experience negative psychological states (such as distress), but as Dorj and her team have noted, emotions in marine mammals, if they truly occur, are probably quite elementary.
